title: Event sourcing
idea: Event sourcing saves every change as an event that is never edited, and computes the current state by replaying the events in order.

analogy.text: A paper ledger. You never erase a line; you add a new one. The balance is whatever the lines add up to.
analogy.breaks: Adding up a short ledger is quick; replaying a long log is slow.

points: Events are facts, such as `Deposited 100`. You only append them, never edit them.
Current state is a reduce over the events: apply each one, oldest first.
Replay only part of the log to see the state at an earlier moment.
Long logs replay slowly, so systems often save snapshots of state along the way.

items.label: Opened
items.text: `Opened` is stored. Replaying it gives balance 0.

items.label: Read the present
items.text: Replay all four events, oldest first, to get the current balance: 120.

items.label: Read the past
items.text: Stop after event 3 to see that the balance was 70 at that moment.

code.title: State from events
code.caption: The events are the stored truth; the balance is recomputed on demand. Change `slice(0, 3)` to see another moment.

pitfalls: Never edit or delete a stored event; append a correcting event instead.
Publishing events is not event sourcing; the stored log itself must be the source of truth.
Old events stay in the log, so new code must still read their old shape.

quiz.why: `slice(0, 3)` replays the first three events: 100 - 30 + 50 = 120. Replaying all four ends at 100.

takeaway: Store what happened; compute the state by replaying it.

starters: How is event sourcing different from just keeping an audit log?
How do snapshots work, and when do I need them?
How do I fix a wrong event if I can never edit it?
